title: Eval anchor decay and cross-rubric transfer calibration protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a formalized protocol (Calibration Transfer Function - CTF) that lets us update or replace rubrics and LLM-judge configurations while preserving historical comparability for quality/regression signals tied to config or model changes. The protocol should combine an anchor-set based decay model, cross-rubric transfer mappings, and temperature/score recalibration steps so that we can safely deploy rubric or judge changes with measurable delta attribution and low false-positive regression alerts.

Why this work matters:
- Frequent rubric and LLM-as-judge tweaks cause noisy downstream alerts and rollback churn when teams cannot compare new scores to historical baselines.
- We need a principled way for the Console and rollout system to report calibrated deltas (not raw judge score differences) so product, SRE, and ML owners can make reliable decisions.

Scope and outcomes:
1) Define Calibration Transfer Function (CTF) specification: mathematical form, required inputs (anchor scores, cohort histograms, model variant mapping), and outputs (score mapping table + uncertainty envelope).
2) Anchor set management: choose anchor cohort size, refresh cadence, and an "anchor-decay" weighting so older anchors contribute less to transfer estimates but retain stability for long-term trend alignment.
3) Cross-rubric transfer: procedures for pairwise mapping between old and new rubric schemas (including label remapping and cost matrix when rubrics are non-isomorphic).
4) Temperature and scaling calibration: automated fit to align score distributions (via isotonic regression or Platt scaling) and propagation of calibration uncertainty to alert thresholds.
5) Integration plan for Console and Rollouts: how calibrated deltas will be surfaced in the Console, gating rules for canary and A/B rollouts, and recommended default behavior for auto-fallback when transfer uncertainty is high.
6) Eval pipeline changes: LLM-as-judge ensemble support, scoring metadata, and storage of transfer provenance for auditability.

Success metrics:
- Decrease in noisy regression alerts attributable to rubric/judge changes by >= 60% within one month of protocol rollout (measured on historical recalculation).
- Mean absolute calibration error between transferred and ground-truth human adjudication reduced to < 3% on held-out anchor cohorts.
- Console shows calibrated delta and uncertainty for 100% of rollout-config changes that touch scoring.

Non-goals:
- Replacing human adjudication for critical safety cohorts (we will still require juried reviews for safety-sensitive cases).
- Building a fully Bayesian uncertainty stack for every model immediately (we will start with bootstrap + isotonic/Platt approaches).

Operational plan and timeline (high level):
- Week 1-2: Draft CTF spec and anchor-decay equation; define anchor cohorts. Deliverable: Confluence spec + anchor cohort list.
- Week 3-4: Implement calibration routines in evals repo; basic transfer mapping utilities. Deliverable: PR for calibration module and unit tests.
- Week 5-6: Integrate with Console signals pipeline; wire up rollout gating. Deliverable: Console UI mocks and backend endpoints.
- Week 7: Internal canary on non-critical model/config changes; measure false-positive alert rate.
- Week 8: Iterate and prepare broader rollout.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Anchor cohorts may not cover rare but high-impact edge cases. Mitigation: Maintain a "safety" juried set excluded from automated transfer; require manual review for any changes affecting those cohorts.
- Risk: Transfer may produce overconfident mappings when rubrics are structurally different. Mitigation: Force a high-uncertainty fallback and require manual calibration when mismatch score > threshold.
- Risk: Additional compute cost for recalculating anchors on every rollout. Mitigation: Use incremental recalculation and sample-based estimation; add batching windows.

Open questions for architecture and eng partners:
- What is the canonical storage format for transfer provenance (we need immutable records linked to rollouts)?
- Should the Console show raw judge scores, calibrated scores, or both by default?
- Acceptable uncertainty thresholds for automatic rollout gating?

Next steps (this ticket):
- PM: finalize CTF spec and schedule design review (Maya) by 2025-02-24.
- Eng: spike on isotonic vs. Platt scaling on our anchor sets (Samir) by 2025-03-03.
- Design: mock Console delta UI with uncertainty bands (Aisha) by 2025-03-05.
